questions.q: How should an investor handle the extreme volatility of crypto prices?
a: Filter out emotion and focus on the long term
Sell immediately whenever the price dips
Check prices many times each day and react fast
Buy more whenever the market sentiment turns negative
questions.why: Lesson 1 advises removing the emotional factor and judging projects over the long run.

questions.q: How large an emergency fund does the summary recommend before investing?
a: Three to six months of expenses
One to two months of expenses
Six to twelve months of expenses
Twelve to eighteen months of expenses
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests covering three to six months of expenses, then investing only what you can afford to lose.

questions.q: Which qualities suggest a cryptocurrency is worth investing in?
a: A strong team, real utility and a limited supply
A funny name, a large following and daily price swings
A recent launch, low price and heavy advertising
A single founder, unlimited supply and no clear use
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists good management, a utility factor and finite supply as signs of a valuable coin.

questions.q: What do smart contracts do, according to lesson 2?
a: They automatically carry out the terms both parties agreed to
They replace the blockchain with a central bank database
They set the market price of a coin each morning
They allow one party to change the agreement at any time
questions.why: Lesson 2 says smart contracts automate execution of an agreement's terms and conditions.

questions.q: What does the author mean by diversification in lesson 3?
a: Holding assets outside crypto too, such as stocks and real estate
Spreading money across as many new coins as possible
Keeping all funds in a single well-reviewed online wallet
Moving between coins whenever one starts to fall
questions.why: Lesson 3 says diversification includes non-crypto assets like stocks, ETFs, bonds and property.
